findings.issue: This is still there: m3 'Stock Styles & Wholesale Buying' and m6 'Pricing & Quotes' are neighbouring check lists, and both put their items beside the heading. The page repeats one arrangement twice in a row, and m6 leaves a tall empty column under its one-line heading.
findings.reference: Site rule: when two neighbouring sections are rows of short items, the template sets only one of them as a list beside its heading.
findings.fix: When two iconList sections are neighbours, have the template give m6 (or m3) the other arrangement, with items in columns under the heading as iconList-1 shows.

findings.issue: This is still there: iconList-1 has no heading and shares m7's tint, so it reads as more of 'Minimum Order Quantities'. Yet its six items jump from m7's single right-hand column to two columns that start on the content's left edge, so one list changes width and starting edge halfway through.
findings.reference: The competitor sets each list of points in one arrangement under its one heading.
findings.fix: When an iconList without a heading follows an iconList of the same tint, have the template treat it as part of that list and keep its arrangement and column (items in the right column beside m7's heading), instead of starting a new grid.

findings.issue: This is still there: the four steps from 'Sign off sample and specs' to 'Bulk production' are an unnumbered table. They sit right above process-1's blue 01–05 steps and below overview-steps, which now numbers its steps 01–06, so this is the only step list on the page without numerals.
findings.reference: The competitor's step modules, including its six-step timeline, put a number on every step, with a bold title over a thin rule.
findings.fix: In the timeline variant of ProcessBlock (.process-timeline__label), show the accent decimal-leading-zero number before each step title, as .point-list__items[data-numbered] does.

findings.issue: This is still there: on phones about 60px of empty space separates 'From sign-off to bulk production' from the first step, and that step has no rule above it, so the heading looks cut off from its list. overview-steps no longer has this gap; it now has a rule above its first step.
findings.reference: The competitor's step lists follow their heading at the usual gap between a heading and its content.
findings.fix: In the single-column layout of .process-timeline, use the heading-to-content gap instead of the side-by-side row gap between the heading and the first row, as overview-steps' list variant now does.

findings.issue: This is still there: in the side column beside its steps, the heading 'Order Confirmation & Scheduling' breaks into three lines, with 'Order' alone on the first. The other side headings on the page (m3, m7, m9) keep to two balanced lines.
findings.reference: The competitor's section headings keep to one or two lines.
findings.fix: Make the template's heading fit allow for the side column's width when it sizes a heading set beside a list, so this one keeps to two lines ('Order Confirmation / & Scheduling'), as it already does on phones.

findings.issue: This is still there: proof-7 has no heading and continues m11 after proof-5 and proof-6, which are at body size, yet its first paragraph ('We measure your packed cartons…') is still in the larger lead size. Phones show the same.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one body size through all the paragraphs of a text section.
findings.fix: Apply .text-flow__lead only to the first paragraph under a section heading, never to the first paragraph of a heading-less block that continues a section.

findings.issue: This is still there: the fee chart draws three identical full-width bars (Sample fee, Design fee and Courier delivery, each $50) that compare nothing, and the two timing bars float on tracks with no axis or scale. On phones the bars shrink to half the card, away from their values.
findings.reference: The competitor shows figures only where they add information.
findings.fix: Have Site Factory give these facts as a short stats row or list (three $50 fees; 10–15 and 5–7 days) instead of bar charts of equal values.

findings.issue: This is still there: the heading 'Related products and services' sits over a single link to 'Case Studies', which is neither a product nor a service, and it is the only heading on the page in sentence case.
findings.fix: Have Site Factory link related product or solution pages here, or retitle the section in Title Case to match its link.
